what: Phase 3b of the estate go-live: the mesh shares what it learns. Phase 3 failed J3 and J4, both kept, from one cause: each asker routed greedily on its own evidence, nothing told the others that a node had gone silent, and nothing made an asker try a holder it had never asked. This pass changes the routing in core/node.mjs and measures the change as new claims on Phase 3's own scenario. Sealed before any of its code exists. Phase 3's claims and receipt are not touched: Phase 3's cells ask for the routing it measured by name, so its receipt still reproduces as sealed.
design: Notes. A node writes a note of what it saw itself: 'silent' when an ask of its own expires unanswered, and 'lied' when a holder answers it VERIFIED with a receipt its own check refuses; a 'lied' note carries the holder's own signed answer packet. A node shares its notes with members as one signed LIGHT message, the way antibodies are shared.

Nothing on the sender's word. A 'lied' note is counted only if the packet it carries is signed by the accused holder's pinned key, is that holder's answer to that ask, was addressed to the note's sender, and fails the receiver's own check; then it counts as one failed answer on the receiver's link. A 'silent' note makes the holder quiet at the receiver at once, so its asks go to another live holder, and the receiver sends the holder a probe: if the holder answers, it is alive and the note changes nothing; if the probe expires unanswered, that counts as a failed answer on the receiver's own link.

Quiet. A holder this node has seen go silent, or been told of and is re-checking, is not live for routing until this node hears from it again. With no live holder of a skill left, the strongest is still tried, as before.

Exploration. Among live holders of a skill, an asker asks one it has never asked itself before one it has, so every asker tries every holder once, within its first k asks of that skill, k the number of holders. It is deterministic: untried first, then the strongest link, then the smaller id.
Phase 3's greedy routing stays as a named mode, routing: 'greedy', and is the control in every run below: the same scenario, seeds and steps, with only the routing changed.
scope: Phase 3's mesh on one machine: eight nodes and two relays, each its own operating-system process, exchanging only bytes over local TCP; fixed public test seeds and a fixed clock, one step at a time. A second device is not claimed here.

The scenario is Phase 3's: four askers, three triage holders of which one is dishonest, one scribe; 100 asks, then the triage holder the asks are actually going to is killed, then 40 triage asks. After each ask, an asker with a new note shares its notes with every other member before the next ask, and probes left unanswered are expired before the next ask. In a deployment the cell does both on a timer; here the driver does them in order so the run is the same on every machine.

The dishonest member in W4 is a pinned member of the roster, and its false notes are written by the measuring code, not by a model. An outside adversary is the owner's to invite; it is not claimed here.

The floor is reached by counting failures: a link starts at 500,000 parts in a million and each failed answer halves it, so four failures take it to 31,250, under the floor of 50,000, and three leave it at 62,500, above it. W2 depends on four askers each finding the dishonest holder once and sharing it; a mesh with fewer askers would need more evidence per asker to cross the floor.

passes.organ: routing that shares what it learns (core/node.mjs: notes, probes, quiet, exploration)

claims.claim: A node that dies is routed around by the whole mesh, not by each asker on its own: the first ask it leaves unanswered warns every other member, so the mesh pays once for finding out (J3, re-measured).
claims.measure: Phase 3's mesh run with the new routing: the triage holder the asks are going to killed after 100 asks, then 40 triage asks; and the same run with Phase 3's greedy routing as the control
claims.holds_if: with the new routing at most 2 asks go to the dead node before every later one goes to a live holder, and every later ask is answered (J3's sealed bar); and with the greedy routing the same run sends more than 2 asks to it, so the scenario can fail
claims.predicted: HOLD — 1 ask, the first asker's; the others are warned before they ask. The control should repeat J3's 4.

claims.claim: Couplings follow evidence at the size of the mesh: a dishonest holder's signed bad answer, seen by one asker, is re-checked and counted by every other, so its link falls at every asker (J4, re-measured).
claims.measure: each of the four askers' links to the live honest triage holder and the dishonest one at the end of the same run, with the new routing and with the greedy control
claims.holds_if: with the new routing, at every asker the honest link is above the dishonest link and the dishonest one is below the floor (J4's sealed bar); and with the greedy routing the dishonest link is not below the floor at some asker, so the scenario can fail
claims.predicted: HOLD — each asker finds the dishonest holder once and counts the other three askers' evidence, four failures in all, 31,250. This holds with four askers and no fewer (see scope). The control should repeat J4's 500,000.

claims.claim: Routing away from a liar is earned, not luck: every asker tries every holder once, so each one asks the dishonest holder itself, once, and then goes to the honest ones (J2, no longer hollow).
claims.measure: the first 100 asks of the same run with the new routing
claims.holds_if: every ask goes to a holder of its skill and all 100 are answered; each of the four askers sends the dishonest holder exactly one ask of its own, within the first 20 asks; and after the first 20, at least 90% of triage asks go to an honest holder
claims.predicted: HOLD — four asks to the dishonest holder in all, one per asker, each by an asker's third triage ask; none after the first 20.

claims.claim: A note moves nothing on its sender's word: false notes from a pinned member change no link anywhere, a holder falsely called silent is live again once it answers the re-check, and notes from a key not on the roster are refused at the door.
claims.measure: a fresh mesh run with the new routing: after every asker has tried every holder, the dishonest member sends each asker a silence note about a live honest holder and four false 'lied' notes about honest holders (one carrying that holder's own honest signed answer, one that answer with a byte changed, one a packet in that holder's name signed by the dishonest member's own key, one naming the other honest holder for that answer); an unpinned stranger sends each asker a silence note; then each asker asks once more
claims.holds_if: 0 links change at any member; every false silence note's probe is answered and no asker holds that holder quiet afterwards; all 16 false 'lied' notes are refused; all 4 of the stranger's notes are refused at the door; and each asker's next triage ask goes to an honest holder and is answered
